links.outcome: Proportion of sepsis ED patients receiving antibiotics within 1 and 3 hours, comparing ML alert versus usual process
links.effect: Antibiotics within 1 h: 68.4% vs 60.1% (P=0.04); within 3 h: 94.5% vs 89.0% (P=0.02); median TTA 46 vs 50 min.
links.quote: The proportions of patients who received antibiotics within 1 and 3 h were higher in the intervention group than in the control group (in 1 h; 68.4 vs. 60.1%, respectively; P = 0.04, in 3 h; 94.5 vs. 89.0%, respectively; P = 0.02).

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance (AUROC) of ML model versus rule-based tools for early sepsis identification
links.effect: ML AUROC significantly higher than qSOFA, SIRS, and MEWS for early sepsis identification.
links.quote: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of ML in early sepsis identification was significantly higher than qSOFA, SIRS, and MEWS.

screen.reason: Cluster-randomized trial evaluating the clinical impact of real-time ML-assisted display alerts versus standard practice for sepsis identification and antibiotic timeliness in an emergency department.
